_comment.1: LOOP DELAY of the y/tip axis, from PRBS bursts: command -> FSM ->
_comment.2: camera -> CoM, cross-correlated against the command that went out.
_comment.3: Same tau conf_bode_par_y.json fits from its 5-200 Hz phase slope,
_comment.4: measured in ~5 s of drive instead of several minutes of sweep.
_comment.5: WHAT TO COPY OUT: the logged PHASE SLOPE line. It is the same
_comment.6: estimator over the same band as bode's fit_tau_ms, so it is what goes
_comment.7: into fsp's y delay/delay_frac pair (delay = whole frames, delay_frac =
_comment.8: the remainder). Peak brackets it from below and onset reads ~0.8
_comment.9: chips EARLY, so quote neither. Do NOT add a
_comment.10: hidden frame here the way bode needs -- this device correlates the
_comment.11: command and the response exactly as the loop sees them: COMPARE IN
_comment.11b: FRAMES against bode fit_frames, never in ms against fit_tau_ms,
_comment.11c: which is one frame (0.26 ms) short by construction.
_comment.12: EXPECT about 2.6 frames: steering_par_fsp.json carries 2+0.62 for y
_comment.13: from fsm_bodey_par2.dat. A result below 1 frame is not a fast loop,
_comment.14: it is a failed measurement (the device says so).
_comment.15: DRIVE: +-50 mV, i.e. +-6 px at Ky 3.646 and 31.5 px/unit -- small
_comment.16: enough to stay in the linear region and inside the 20x20 tracking
_comment.17: window, since SNR here comes from averaging 64 bursts, not from
_comment.18: amplitude. One frame per chip on purpose: a chip is a boxcar, and a
_comment.19: chip longer than the delay smears the onset by its own length.
_comment.20: 127 chips + 128 quiet = 255 frames per burst, x64 = ~4.3 s at 3.8 kHz.
_comment.21: See conf_prbs_par_x.json for the x/tilt twin, and conf_gain_par_y.json
_comment.22: for the gain half of the same plant.

params._roi_note: ROI and exposure copied from steering_par_fsp.json so this measures the plant the loop actually runs against. Exposure is part of the delay being measured: change it and this number changes.

params._note: tracked 20x20, threshold 5, min_peak 40 -- the steering configuration exactly. The centroid computation is inside the delay being measured, so it has to be the same one the loop uses.

pipeline._note1: THE TEST. Drives element 0 (y) and watches element 0 of the CoM ([y, x]); x stays at 0 command, i.e. parked at 0 V.
pipeline._note2: quiet_frames 128 is both the rest between bursts (so each one starts from the same state) and the room the correlator needs: it must be at least max_lag, or one burst's tail overlaps the next burst's start.
pipeline._note3: neg_lags 24 buys the noise floor. Nothing can respond before the command, so the scatter over those acausal lags is what the onset threshold and the peak/noise ratio are judged against. It is not just sensor noise -- the linear autocorrelation of a finite 127-chip m-sequence has sidelobes of a few percent.
pipeline._phase_band: 20-200 Hz. The top matches the freq_end of the x sweep (conf_bode_par_y.json's own sweep stops at 100 Hz; 200 keeps both axes' tau fit over one band), so this tau and that one are fit over the same band and are directly comparable. Raising phase_f_hi past the plant's own roll-off starts fitting noise, not delay.

params.config: y/tip loop delay through the PARPORT DAC (DAC81404, spi link, mmio, +-5 V range, mirror parked at 0 V), no coarse stage, ch0=y driven at scale 1.0 V/unit / ch1=x parked. 64x64 ROI 644/318, exp 400, gain 0, tracked 20x20 thr 5 min_peak 40. Compare the phase-slope tau IN FRAMES against fsm_bodey_par2.dat's 2.624 fr (that file's 0.4288 ms EXCLUDES bode's hidden frame and is not what this device reports) and against the fsp delay/delay_frac in steering_par_fsp.json.

pipeline._note: PARPORT DAC, wired exactly as steering_par_fsp.json: ch0 = y/tip, ch1 = x/tilt, scale [1, -1], offset 0. skip_unchanged stays off -- a PRBS changes the code every frame anyway, and a skipped write would be a missing edge in the very stimulus being correlated.
pipeline._range: +-5 fixed, no auto-ranging: a range change mid-burst would put a one-frame glitch into the response and land in the correlogram as a spurious lag.
